article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Kush × Afghani × NYC Diesel × G13 Haze
Breeder: Soma’s Sacred Seeds
THC Content: 23%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: caryophyllene , myrcene , limonene
Primary Flavors: Sweet fruit, flowers, incense, spice
Flowering Time (Indoor): H12–13 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: mid-November to mid-December
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: High potential
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Somini occupies one of the less frequently discussed corners of Soma Seeds’ catalog, yet its pedigree contains several of the breeder’s most recognizable influences. Kush and Afghani genetics supply resin, spice, and traditional hash character, while NYC Diesel and G13 Haze push the plant toward taller growth, a more cerebral effect, and a noticeably more exotic aromatic profile. Historical descriptions identify Somini as a vigorous sativa-dominant marijuana variety with an open structure, thin foliage, generous branching, and large resinous flowers that may acquire lavender tones near maturity.

Its aroma moves well beyond straightforward Kush, mixing sweetness and fruit with flowers, incense, and spice. Surviving breeder-derived listings describe the effect as powerful, cerebral, and long-lasting, particularly suited to social recreation rather than immediate sedation. Somini is therefore best understood as an old-school Soma hybrid built for connoisseurs willing to accept a longer flowering schedule in exchange for complex smoke, resin production, and an expansive sativa-style experience.
Genetics and Lineage

The most detailed surviving description identifies Somini as a combination of Kush, Afghani, NYC Diesel, and G13 Haze genetics. It is attributed directly to Soma Seeds and classified as sativa-dominant. That four-part genetic structure explains why the plant does not resemble a conventional Kush despite carrying Kush and Afghan ancestry. The G13 Haze and NYC Diesel portions pull strongly toward longer internodal spacing, thinner leaves, extended flowering, and a cerebral high, while the Afghan and Kush components reinforce resin production and add heavier spice and hash aromas.

NYC Diesel is itself one of Soma’s signature sativa-leaning cultivars, famous for an exotic grapefruit-like fragrance and an energetic high. G13 Haze contributes another layer of Haze intensity and extended maturation. In Somini, those more expansive genetics are counterweighted by denser, resin-oriented Afghan and Kush characteristics. The result is not a perfectly even compromise. Plant morphology and historical descriptions indicate that the sativa side remains dominant, particularly in height, branch spacing, flower structure, and effect.

Somini also appears to have become comparatively rare within the modern Soma catalog. Current breeder directories still identify it as a Soma Seeds creation, while some contemporary seed retailers list the old regular seed version as unavailable or out of stock. That relative scarcity makes provenance important when encountering flower or seeds carrying the Somini name today.
Effects and Experience

The experience develops primarily through the head. Historical descriptions characterize Somini as powerful, cerebral, and long-lasting, which fits the combination of NYC Diesel and G13 Haze ancestry. Moderate consumption can bring a noticeable lift in mood, greater interest in conversation, and a freer, more associative style of thinking. Social settings are particularly compatible with the cultivar because the mental stimulation can make music, humor, storytelling, or casual discussion feel more absorbing without immediately producing the physical shutdown associated with heavy indica marijuana.

A warmer body sensation can emerge later, especially in phenotypes expressing more of the Kush and Afghani background. That physical layer usually acts as a foundation rather than the central feature of the high. Larger amounts may make the cerebral effects hazier and reduce concentration, while consumers sensitive to stimulating weed could experience restlessness or anxiety if dosage is excessive.

Reliable THC values are difficult to establish. Modern databases assign widely conflicting potency ranges, which is a good example of why strain-wide cannabinoid percentages should not be treated as permanent genetic specifications. The breeder material available for Somini emphasizes strength rather than one laboratory number. Consumers should therefore rely on testing from the actual batch whenever possible.
Medical Benefits

Somini’s mentally uplifting character may interest medical cannabis consumers who prefer a cultivar that remains relatively functional instead of immediately becoming sedative. Sativa-dominant marijuana with this type of progression is sometimes chosen during periods of stress, low mood, reduced motivation, or mental fatigue. The underlying Kush and Afghan influence may also provide enough bodily relaxation to make the experience feel less sharp than a pure tropical Haze.

No clinical evidence demonstrates that Somini itself treats depression, anxiety, chronic pain, nausea, or another medical condition. Claims attached to individual strain names are largely experiential and cannot substitute for standardized cannabis research. Chemical variation is another consideration: an old seed-derived cultivar can produce multiple phenotypes with different cannabinoid and terpene levels.

Higher doses of THC may also create unwanted effects, including dizziness, dry mouth, impaired concentration, rapid heartbeat, or anxiety. Medical consumers should pay attention to the cannabinoid analysis of the specific product and seek professional guidance when using cannabis for persistent symptoms.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Somini has one of the more layered aromatic profiles among older Soma strains. Historical descriptions emphasize sweetness, fruit, flowers, incense, and spice rather than one dominant flavor. The first impression from cured buds can be floral and slightly fruity, but breaking the flower apart releases a darker mixture of earth, hash, dry herbs, and peppery spice. Incense becomes particularly noticeable in some expressions, tying the strain back to its Haze ancestry.

On inhalation, sweet fruit and floral notes may appear before the smoke develops a warmer, spicier center. The finish can lean toward earthy Kush and hash, especially in flowers expressing more Afghan influence. Compared with modern dessert marijuana, Somini tastes decidedly traditional. Its sweetness is botanical rather than candy-like, surrounded by resin, spice, and incense.

No authoritative standardized terpene panel was published for the original cultivar. Caryophyllene could plausibly account for pepper and spice, myrcene for earthy or fruity depth, limonene for brighter fruit tones, and linalool for floral qualities. Those are sensory associations rather than confirmed strain-wide chemistry, however, and laboratory testing remains necessary to identify the dominant terpenes in any specific harvest.
Growing Information

Somini develops as a large, open cannabis plant with considerable spacing between nodes and relatively narrow leaves. Historical cultivation information describes vigorous growth and numerous lateral branches capable of supporting large, somewhat airy but resinous flowers. The low proportion of leaf to flower can make mature buds easier to manicure, while lavender coloration may emerge near the end of bloom.

Indoor growers should keep the vegetative period relatively short because the plant’s sativa influence can produce substantial stretch once flowering begins. Topping, low-stress training, or a screen can help redirect vertical growth and distribute the long branches beneath the lighting. A wider canopy also suits the plant’s natural open structure. Because flowers tend to remain less compact than dense Kush buds, airflow through the canopy is generally easier to maintain, although humidity should still be controlled carefully.

Flowering time is one area where surviving sources conflict. A detailed historical listing gives approximately 12–13 weeks indoors and an outdoor finish between mid-November and mid-December, while some current retailers reproduce much shorter estimates of eight to ten or nine to ten weeks. The discrepancy may reflect different generations, selected phenotypes, or inaccurate modern catalog copying. For the original sativa-dominant Somini description, growers should be prepared for the longer schedule.

Outdoors, a Mediterranean-style climate is ideal because plants need warmth and enough autumn to finish properly. Somini is vigorous and productive when given sufficient root space and sunlight, but its late maturity makes it a risky choice for regions where cold rain or frost arrives early.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Somini?

Somini is a Soma Seeds hybrid combining Kush, Afghani, NYC Diesel, and G13 Haze genetics. The sativa influence from NYC Diesel and G13 Haze is especially evident in its plant structure and cerebral effects.
Is Somini indica or sativa?
Somini is best classified as a sativa-dominant hybrid. Historical descriptions emphasize tall growth, thin leaves, open internodal spacing, long flowering, and a powerful cerebral high.
What does Somini taste like?

The flavor combines sweet fruit, flowers, incense, spice, earth, and hash-like notes. Its profile is more complex and botanical than the candy-oriented flavors associated with many modern cannabis strains.
How long does Somini take to flower?

The most detailed historical description gives approximately 12–13 weeks indoors. Some later retailers list eight to ten or nine to ten weeks, so phenotype and seed provenance may significantly affect maturation time.
Is Somini good for outdoor growing?

Yes, provided the climate offers a long, warm season. Historical information specifically recommends Mediterranean-style outdoor conditions, with the original expression potentially finishing from mid-November into December.
Final Thoughts on Somini

Somini represents Soma Seeds at its most genetically eclectic. Kush and Afghan material provide resin and old-school hash depth, while NYC Diesel and G13 Haze give the plant its open sativa architecture, cerebral power, and exotic floral-incense character. The result is marijuana that feels distinctly different from the compact, fast-finishing hybrids dominating much of today’s seed market.

Its long maturation period is the principal compromise. Growers working with authentic or older expressions may need twelve weeks or more of flowering, substantial vertical space, and enough patience to allow the aromatic qualities to develop fully. In return, the cultivar offers vigorous branching, resinous flowers, relatively little leaf, possible lavender coloration, and a strong social high with considerable duration.

For enthusiasts exploring the lesser-known branches of Soma Seeds history, Somini deserves attention precisely because it does not follow a simple formula. It combines several influential genetic families into a tall, fragrant, sativa-oriented plant whose sweet fruit, flowers, incense, spice, and hash character reflect the diversity of its ancestry.
